note: Blackbody-radiation (BBR) sensitivities are approximate: dν/ν per kelvin at 300 K, obtained from the room-temperature BBR shift with T⁴ scaling.
performance_note: Representative values per performance class. σᵧ(1 s) is the instability of one clock; comparing it with an identical reference clock is √2 noisier. The systematic uncertainty is incurred again at every station set-up and does not average down. Uptime is the fraction of time the clock produces valid data.

performance_classes.label: Field-demonstrated
performance_classes.description: Transportable clocks as operated outside the laboratory today.

performance_classes.label: Laboratory state of the art
performance_classes.description: Best stationary laboratory performance. Not yet demonstrated with a transportable clock.

performance_classes.label: Projected
performance_classes.description: An assumption about future field clocks. Not demonstrated anywhere.

field.basis: Transportable ⁸⁷Sr lattice clocks operated outside the laboratory: systematic uncertainty from 7 × 10⁻¹⁷ (PTB, 2017) to the 10⁻¹⁸ level (RIKEN, 2020–2021), instability of order 10⁻¹⁶–10⁻¹⁵ /√τ. Uptime is an assumption.

laboratory.basis: Stationary ⁸⁷Sr lattice clocks: 4.8 × 10⁻¹⁷ /√τ (JILA, 2019); systematic uncertainty 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁸ (JILA, 2019) and 8 × 10⁻¹⁹ (JILA, 2024).

projected.basis: Assumption: a field clock about one order of magnitude better than today's best laboratory clocks. Not demonstrated.

field.basis: No transportable ¹⁷¹Yb field campaign is modelled; values are assumed equal to transportable ⁸⁷Sr clocks.

laboratory.basis: Stationary ¹⁷¹Yb lattice clocks (NIST, 2017–2018): instability about 10⁻¹⁶ /√τ, systematic uncertainty 1.4 × 10⁻¹⁸.

projected.basis: Assumption: a field clock about one order of magnitude better than today's best laboratory clocks. Not demonstrated.

field.basis: Transportable ion clocks are under development; no field campaign is modelled. Values are assumed.

laboratory.basis: Stationary ²⁷Al⁺ quantum-logic clock (NIST, 2019): instability 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ /√τ, systematic uncertainty 9.4 × 10⁻¹⁹.

projected.basis: Assumption: a multi-ion field clock. Not demonstrated.

field.basis: Commercial caesium-beam frequency standards: instability about 10⁻¹¹ /√τ, accuracy about 5 × 10⁻¹³.

laboratory.basis: Caesium fountain primary standards: instability about 10⁻¹³ /√τ, systematic uncertainty about 2 × 10⁻¹⁶.

projected.basis: No projection: microwave clocks are not expected to reach optical-clock performance, so fountain values are used.
